schema._doc: Reference only — not a real home. Copy this shape, drop the _doc keys. Use null for anything unverified; NEVER guess a number. Most listing fields come straight from a Firecrawl scrape of the Zillow page.

schema.rejectedReason: null unless status is rejected — which hard parameter failed
schema.verdict: One or two plain sentences: what this house is and what we should do about it. The first thing the family reads.

scores._doc: Keys match criterion ids in data/rubric.json. 0-5, or null for unknown. Every score needs a why citing the transcript tag.

flags._doc: Plain-language red flags. Severity drives the colour on the site.

monthly.note: Insurance is a generic estimate, not a quote. In a wildfire zone this line could be 3-4x higher.

homes.verdict: A 1963 fixer at $375k, 6.5 minutes from YWAM, with 5 bedrooms, a basement kitchenette, no HOA, and only $1,535 a year in tax — and the county values it $103k ABOVE the asking price. The catch is real though: it's sold as-is and the seller excluded FHA and VA financing, which usually means the condition wouldn't pass those appraisals. Worth touring, but bring a contractor, not just an inspector.

listing.basement: Partial, partially finished — includes a second kitchenette
listing.floodZone: FEMA Zone X — moderate-risk flood area
listing.listingTerms: Cash, Conventional only — no FHA, no VA

foundation.why: No structural information at all — 1963 build on Front Range clay, sold as-is, no engineering report mentioned. Genuinely unknown, so scored null rather than guessed [T04]

wildfire.why: East of I-25, no foothills interface, outside every wildland-urban interface neighborhood named in the videos. Insurance should price normally here [T04][T06]

water.why: FEMA Zone X moderate-risk — not federally mandated coverage but not minimal either. Grading and basement moisture unverified [T04]

roof.why: Composite shingle, age not stated, on a 1963 house sold as-is. Not Class 4, so no premium discount. Assume replacement at $11-25k [T04]

systems.why: 1963 build puts galvanized supply pipe, aluminum branch wiring, and a clay or cast-iron sewer lateral all in play. Listing itemises only cosmetic work, so mechanicals are unverified [T04]

layout.why: 5 beds and 3 baths beats our 4/3 minimum, plus a dedicated office, oversized garage, storage shed, and a basement kitchenette that gives the separate-suite option [T08]

value.why: $154/sqft, and the county's actual value is $478,587 against a $375k ask. Even adding $90k of renovation lands near $465k, well under our $600k ceiling

location.why: 6.5 min to YWAM is good, but Walk Score 23 is car-dependent and it's marketed as UCCS student-rental territory. Driveway orientation and sun exposure unknown [T07]

carrying.why: No HOA, no metro district, municipal water on one CSU bill, and only $1,535/yr in tax. About as clean as carrying costs get here [T07][T06]

radon.why: No test mentioned. Partial basement. El Paso County is EPA Zone 1, so assume it needs testing [BASE]

resale.why: Built-out area with no new construction competing, which is the appreciation lever [T08]. But cash/conventional-only shrinks the buyer pool until the condition is fixed

financing.text: Sold as-is, and the seller excluded FHA and VA — cash or conventional only. That usually means the condition wouldn't pass an FHA or VA appraisal, and it shrinks the pool of buyers when we eventually sell.

era.text: Built 1963. Galvanized supply pipe, aluminum branch wiring, and a clay or cast-iron sewer lateral are all in play at that age. Scope the sewer and open the electrical panel before the inspection deadline.

roof.text: Composite shingle with no stated age on a 1963 house. Budget $11,000-25,000, and it won't be Class 4 — so no insurance discount either.

flood.text: FEMA Zone X, moderate-risk flood area. Coverage isn't federally required, but get a quote and look hard at how the ground slopes around the foundation.

investor.text: Marketed to investors as UCCS student housing. Expect rental-heavy neighbours and competition from investors on any offer — 1,409 views and 102 saves in 36 days.

upside.text: The county values this at $478,587 against a $375,000 ask — about $103k of headroom. The bones may genuinely be worth more than the price.

carrying.text: No HOA, no metro district, municipal water, and $1,535 a year in tax. Carrying costs are excellent, which is rarer than it sounds around here.

monthly.note: Assumes 20% down ($300k loan) at 6.5% over 30 years — confirm the rate with a lender. Insurance is an estimate from the Colorado statewide average, NOT a quote. This one is outside the wildfire zones, so it should price normally, but get the real number before the deadline.

offer.rationale: 36 days on market with one cut already ($385k to $375k), and the seller is selling as-is. Push on price rather than repairs — an as-is investor listing that excluded FHA/VA won't have appetite for a repair addendum. Counterweight: 102 saves and investor demand mean a deep lowball probably won't land, so $350k is a real offer rather than a fishing expedition.
asks: Price credit for the roof instead of asking them to replace it — they're selling as-is [T04]
Full inspection contingency with enough days for a sewer scope and a structural engineer
Rate buydown over a further price cut if they push back — often saves more monthly [T05]

openQuestions: Roof age, and is there a permit for the last replacement?
Has a structural engineer ever evaluated it? 1963 on Front Range clay, sold as-is
Sewer lateral material — scope it regardless
Electrical panel brand, and is there aluminum branch wiring?
Insurance quote for this exact address
Why cash/conventional only — what specifically would fail an FHA appraisal?
How many of the 5 bedrooms are conforming with proper egress windows?
Get a contractor walkthrough for the real renovation number before the deadline
